hip:32349.name: Sirius
hip:32349.text: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, just eight point six light years away. It has a faint companion, a white dwarf the size of Earth.

hip:30438.name: Canopus
hip:30438.text: Canopus is the second brightest star in the sky. Spacecraft have used it as a fixed point to keep their bearings.

hip:69673.name: Arcturus
hip:69673.text: Arcturus is an orange giant thirty seven light years away. Follow the curve of the Big Dipper's handle and arc to Arcturus.

hip:91262.name: Vega
hip:91262.text: Vega, in Lyra, is twenty five light years away. In about twelve thousand years, Earth's wobble will make it our pole star.

hip:24608.name: Capella
hip:24608.text: Capella looks like one star, but it is two pairs of stars, forty three light years away, shining as one golden point.

hip:24436.name: Rigel
hip:24436.text: Rigel marks Orion's foot. It is a blue supergiant hundreds of light years away, tens of thousands of times brighter than the Sun.

hip:37279.name: Procyon
hip:37279.text: Procyon's name means before the dog: it rises just before Sirius, the Dog Star. It is only eleven light years away.

hip:27989.name: Betelgeuse
hip:27989.text: Betelgeuse is the red shoulder of Orion, a supergiant so large it would swallow the orbit of Mars. In 2020 it dimmed so much that astronomers wondered if it was about to explode.

hip:97649.name: Altair
hip:97649.text: Altair spins so fast, about once every nine hours, that it bulges at its equator. It is seventeen light years away.

hip:21421.name: Aldebaran
hip:21421.text: Aldebaran is the orange eye of Taurus the bull. It looks like part of the Hyades cluster around it, but it is much closer to us.

hip:80763.name: Antares
hip:80763.text: Antares is the red heart of Scorpius. Its name means rival of Mars, because the two look so alike.

hip:65474.name: Spica
hip:65474.text: Spica, in Virgo, is two hot blue stars orbiting each other so closely they are stretched into egg shapes.

hip:37826.name: Pollux
hip:37826.text: Pollux is the brighter twin in Gemini, an orange giant with a planet of its own.

hip:102098.name: Deneb
hip:102098.text: Deneb, the tail of Cygnus the swan, is one of the most luminous stars you can see. It is so far away that its distance is still uncertain.

hip:11767.name: Polaris
hip:11767.text: Polaris, the North Star, sits less than one degree from the celestial pole, so the whole northern sky seems to turn around it.

hip:113368.name: Fomalhaut
hip:113368.text: Fomalhaut is often called the lonely star of autumn, bright in an empty part of the sky. A ring of dust circles it.

hip:49669.name: Regulus
hip:49669.text: Regulus is the heart of Leo. It sits so close to the Sun's path that the Moon often passes right in front of it.

moon.name: The Moon
moon.text: The Moon always shows us the same face. The dark patches you can see are old seas of lava, billions of years old.

planet:jupiter.name: Jupiter
planet:jupiter.text: Jupiter is the largest planet. Hold a pair of binoculars steady and you can see up to four of its moons in a line beside it.

planet:saturn.name: Saturn
planet:saturn.text: Saturn looks like a steady golden star. Even a small telescope shows its rings.

planet:mars.name: Mars
planet:mars.text: Mars gets its colour from rusted iron in its dust. Every two years it swings close to Earth and shines brighter.

planet:venus.name: Venus
planet:venus.text: Venus is the brightest planet, wrapped in thick cloud. Through binoculars you can see it show phases, like a tiny moon.

dso:NGC 1976.name: The Orion Nebula
dso:NGC 1976.text: The fuzzy patch in Orion's sword is the Orion Nebula, a nursery where new stars are forming, more than a thousand light years away.

dso:M 45.name: The Pleiades
dso:M 45.text: The Pleiades, or Seven Sisters, is a cluster of young blue stars. Most people can count six; dark skies show many more.

dso:NGC 224.name: The Andromeda Galaxy
dso:NGC 224.text: The Andromeda Galaxy is about two and a half million light years away. The light you see left it before our species existed.
